contentBlocks.body: fetch resolves for every HTTP status, including 404 and 500, and response.json() is typed any. A thin wrapper fixes both: it returns a discriminated union describing every outcome, so callers must handle not-found, validation errors, and server failures instead of only the happy path.

Split the wrapper into an impure shell (the fetch call) and a pure core (status plus body in, ApiResult out). The pure core holds every decision and can be unit-tested with plain objects, no mocking of fetch required.

Decide which failures are retryable up front. 429 Too Many Requests and 5xx server errors may succeed later; 4xx client errors such as 404 or 422 will fail the same way every time, so retrying them only adds load.

knowledgeItems.prompt: What does await fetch(url) do when the server responds 404?

payload.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failures. HTTP error statuses resolve, so you must check res.status or res.ok yourself.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which status is it reasonable to retry automatically?

payload.explanation: 503 is a temporary server condition. The 4xx statuses describe a problem with the request that a retry will not fix.

payload.text: Keeping the status-to-result mapping in a ____ function lets you test it without mocking fetch.
